speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked the Minister for Health with regard to the law imposing a cohort smoking ban that was recently passed in New Zealand (a) whether the Ministry can provide an update on whether the study on how the ban can be applied to Singapore has been completed; and (b) if so, when will the findings be published.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether an update can be provided on the study to impose a cohort smoking ban, which is similar to the recent ban imposed by New Zealand; (b) what are the issues that will be faced in its implementation; and (c) how soon can this cohort smoking ban be implemented.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Speaker, may I answer Question Nos 1 and 2 together?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: MOH is continually reviewing and enhancing our anti-smoking measures.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This includes studying international practices and ideas on how to further reduce smoking prevalence.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Nevertheless, it is an interesting policy move that is worth studying further to see if it is appropriate and effective in Singapore’s context.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The question is apart from doing a generation ban, we have moved up the age limit to 21 years.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Is MOH considering moving the age limit even higher?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As Dr Lim Wee Kiak rightly pointed out, it is not that we are not doing anything.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There are a lot of other things, including legislation and all that.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have to look at all these concurrently and see what is the impact it has made over the past few years.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In respect of that particular issue, it is something that we will constantly review to see what is the effectiveness of doing so, in light of all the different measures that we have already in place.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I can understand that the Government will have to be very careful in deliberating and it may take awhile.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But we also know the ill effects of smoking and second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It is without a doubt, indisputable why we should curb smoking and second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I want to ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary why is the hesitation still there and what can be the downside to having a cohort ban on smoking?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Now that we have been pushing for Healthier SG, would MOH not see this as a longer-term Healthier SG move, so that there is a structural shift towards better public health for the public and for the individual as well?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As mentioned, we are not closing our minds to this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In fact, we are reviewing it but we are also learning to see how it is going to be effective in our context.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: At this juncture, if we are looking New Zealand, they are actually not banning vaping and we have a certain strong position on vaping because we know that that is the start to a lot of the addiction to tobacco.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are not closing to door to this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As with everything, we want to make sure that it is effective because it is also the implementation, the resources that we have to put in.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We must make that whatever, we do generates the outcome that we desire and we are not just paying lip service to it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: That is where the effort is being put; to see, in conjunction with all the things that are already in place, how effective can this be and how can we tweak it to suit the purposes that we need at this juncture.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Could I ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary one question?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Is the Government setting itself any timeline to review this?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: As the other hon Member Dr Lim has mentioned, other countries are already looking into it and have expressed intention to introduce it.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: So, is the Government setting any timeline to review this prospect of having a generational ban?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I can assure the Member that these issues are alive.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As Mr Liang alluded to, we are rolling out Healthier SG and different components of Healthier SG are things we are constantly looking at.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We do need to see, insofar as what happens in other countries, what the outcomes there are.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As it stands, we are already constantly reviewing, constantly taking in feedback from partners that we are working with to see how best we can implement this.
